name: Gargantua

attributes.attribute: opened a cask that flooded the earth

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Gargantua was a Continental Celtic god. The French author Rabelais drew on him when he created the best-known giant in French literature. The god may have been named Gurgiunt or Gargam originally. Gargantua lived in the otherworld. He broke through to the mortal world from time to time. He created landscapes by tossing rocks around. He could also open a cask of water. The floodwaters then covered the earth.

okr.objective: Record Gargantua as an obscure Celtic god source for a famous literary giant.
key_results: Rabelais based his famous giant on Gargantua.

He opened a cask whose floodwaters covered the earth.
